claims.text: Traditional EAM reference potentials inadequately represent the many atomic configurations of ab initio high-entropy-alloy liquids.
The limited configuration representation of EAM references causes substantial thermodynamic-integration path mismatch in the liquid state.
An MLP trained on representative ab initio molecular-dynamics liquid configurations can replace the traditional EAM reference.
The proposed intervention is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys, particularly equimolar systems.
The proposed intervention is applicable near the high melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
Liquid-like configurations are prominent near melting.
Many-body interactions become significant near the melting point of these alloys.
An MLP can capture a broader range of atomic configurations than conventional EAM or two-body models.
An MLP can capture more complex bonding environments than conventional EAM or two-body models.
Training directly on ab initio liquid configurations will make the MLP reproduce the liquid-phase ab initio energy landscape more accurately.
More accurate reproduction of the liquid energy landscape will increase reference–target phase-space overlap.
Increased reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Ab initio training data can enable the MLP to capture non-trivial multielement interactions in high-entropy alloys.
The MLP reference is expected to improve free-energy calculation accuracy relative to the EAM reference.
The path mismatch may be reduced by an amount on the order of tens of percent.
High-entropy-alloy phase stability involves a complex interplay among mixing enthalpy, intermetallic formation, and melting point.
Applicability at much lower temperatures is uncertain because EAM references may suffice there.
Comparing EAM- and MLP-referenced thermodynamic integration against ab initio free energies can test the proposed improvement.
